questions.question: Distinguish between traditional and symbolic logic
questions.solution_html:
• Tradiitonal logic: Based on Aristotelean logic
  • Uses ordinary language
  • Unit of analysis is terms
  • Limited to simple forms of reasoning
  • Symbolic logic: Based on modern mathematical logic
  • Uses symbols
  • Unit of analysis is proposition
  • Involves simple and complex reasoning

  • Betty is elected Vice president be q
  • Carol is treasurer be r

questions.question: Critically examine the limitations of propositional logic and explain how predicate logic overcomes them.
questions.solution_html:
• Propositional logic
  •  Treats whole proposition as single unit.
  •  Lacks Internal analysis.
  •  Statements involving generality cannot be expressed
  • Predicate logic
  •  Internal analysis is possible
  •  Uses quantifiers to express generality
  •  Relationship between terms are expressed
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss how constants and variables are used in propositional logic and predicate logic. Illustrate
questions.solution_html:
• In propositional logic
  • Constants represent whole propositions
  • Denoted by capital letters
  • Eg P Q
  • Variables represent unspecified propositions
  • It is rarely used
  • In predicate logic
  • Constants represent specific individuals or objects
  • Eg, R, S
  • Variables represent arbitrary objects
  • Eg. x, y
